column1: # GPIO_5 / GPIO_6 carry TWO claims.  This file assigns them to the SDIO
# data bus; cc3501e-bridge-firmware ti/cc3501e_aen_wifi.syscfg pins
# CONFIG_UART2_0 TX/RX to the same pads and
# hal/ti/cc3501e_hw_ti_gpio.c reserves them.  On the DEFAULT SPI build
# that is harmless -- the syscfg says the bridge has no physical console
# and never calls InitTerm()/Report(), so the UART2 instance is a
# link-time stub.  With CC3501E_CONTROL_TRANSPORT=sdio, a supported
# build option, both claims are on the same silicon pads with no
# arbitration and no build-time check: that build needs the UART2 stub
# moved to pads the SDIO bus does not use (#1808).
# SPI data pads CORRECTED 2026-08-30 (#1807).  This file used to pair
# Alif MOSI with CC3501E GPIO_28 and MISO with GPIO_29, which is
# backwards: the CC35xx fixes SPI0_PICO (peripheral data IN) on GPIO_29
# and SPI0_POCI (peripheral data OUT) on GPIO_28 -- GPIO_28 is not a
# legal PICO assignment -- so as written the master's output landed on
# the slave's output pin and neither data direction had a driver.
# The BOARD is not wrong and needs NO rework.  The E1M-AEN-2626-R2
# module netlist (alp-sdk-internal) routes Alif P14_5 (SPI1_MOSI_C)
# through series resistor R62 to CC3501E GPIO_29, and P14_4
# (SPI1_MISO_C) through R48 to GPIO_28 -- i.e. exactly the pairing the
# silicon requires and exactly what cc3501e-bridge-firmware assigns
# (picoPin = GPIO29, pociPin = GPIO28).  Only this table was wrong.
# The HARDWARE NOTE in the firmware's ti/cc3501e_aen.syscfg, which calls
# this a SoM rev bug needing a cross-wire rework, is stale for R2 and
# should be read against that netlist before it is believed.
signal
SPI1_SCLK
SPI1_MOSI
column2: SPI0_PICO / GPIO_29 (CC35 SPI0 slave data IN)

column1: SPI1_MISO
column2: SPI0_POCI / GPIO_28 (CC35 SPI0 slave data OUT)

column2: SDIO.D0 / GPIO_5 (also CONFIG_UART2_0 TX in the bridge syscfg)
